extracted.intended_audience: state officials seeking an FDCPA exemption; debt collectors, compliance officers, and their attorneys/regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory criteria, procedural requirements, and official commentary from CFPB Regulation F concerning (a) how a State may apply for an exemption from certain FDCPA provisions and (b) key definitions and communication rules for FDCPA debt collectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant State law
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant State law means the State law that, for a class of debt collection practices within that State, is claimed to contain requirements that are substantially similar to the requirements that relevant Federal law imposes on that class of debt collection practices, and that contains adequate provision for State enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State law includes State statutes, any regulations that implement State statutes, and formal interpretations of State statutes or regulations by a court of competent jurisdiction or duly authorized State agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class of debt collection practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Class of debt collection practices includes one or more such classes of debt collection practices referred to in paragraph I(b)(1) of this appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant Federal law (for exemption determinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant Federal law means sections 803 through 812 of the Act (15 U.S.C. 1692a through 1692j) and the corresponding provisions of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirements (who, how, and where to file)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State may apply in writing to the Assistant Director, Office of Regulations, Division of Research, Monitoring, and Regulations, Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection, signed by the Governor, Attorney General, or State official having primary enforcement responsibility under the State law that applies to the class of debt collection practices, and supported by the documents specified in this appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application may be submitted in paper or electronic form and must be addressed to the specified Assistant Director/office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting document: copy of applicant State law
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be accompanied by a copy of the applicant State law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be submitted in paper or electronic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting document: comparison of State and Federal provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A comparison of each provision of relevant Federal law with the corresponding provisions of the applicant State law, together with reasons supporting the claim that the corresponding provisions of the applicant State law are substantially similar to the provisions of relevant Federal law, and an explanation as to why any differences ... are not inconsistent with ... Federal law and do not result in a diminution in the protection otherwise afforded consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must also include a statement that no other State laws (including administrative or judicial interpretations) are related to, or would have an effect upon, the State law that is being considered by the Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting document: comparison of enforcement provisions with §814
rubrics_metrics.description: A comparison of the provisions of the State law that provide for enforcement with the provisions of section 814 of the Act (15 U.S.C. 1692l), together with reasons supporting the claim that the applicant State law provides for adequate administrative enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting document: statement identifying designated enforcement office and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying the office designated or to be designated to enforce the applicant State law that shows how the office provides for adequate enforcement, including necessary facilities, personnel, and funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include complete information regarding fiscal arrangements for administrative enforcement (amounts of funds available or to be provided), the number and qualifications of personnel engaged or to be engaged in enforcement, and a description of the procedures under which the applicant State law is to be enforced by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary comparison approach for determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau primarily will consider each provision of the applicant State law in comparison with each corresponding provision in relevant Federal law, and not the State law as a whole in comparison with the Act as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau will consider the criteria set forth and any other relevant information in making its determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial similarity: definitions and rules of construction
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for the applicant State law to be substantially similar to relevant Federal law, the applicant State law at least must provide that definitions and rules of construction, as applicable, import a meaning and have an application that are substantially similar to those prescribed by relevant Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial similarity: required notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant State law must require that debt collectors provide all of the applicable notices required by relevant Federal law, with the content and in the terminology, form, and time periods prescribed pursuant to relevant Federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau may determine whether additional notice requirements under the applicant State law affect a determination that the applicant State law is substantially similar to relevant Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial similarity: affirmative actions and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must take all affirmative actions and abide by obligations substantially similar to those prescribed by relevant Federal law under substantially similar conditions and within substantially similar time periods as are prescribed under relevant Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial similarity: prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must abide by prohibitions that are substantially similar to those prescribed by relevant Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial similarity: consumer obligations burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers' obligations or responsibilities must be no more costly, lengthy, or burdensome than consumers' corresponding obligations or responsibilities under relevant Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial similarity: consumers' rights and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers' rights and protections must be substantially similar to those provided by relevant Federal law under conditions or within time periods that are substantially similar to those prescribed by relevant Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-adverse treatment of additional State requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In applying the substantial similarity criteria, the Bureau will not consider adversely any additional requirements of State law that are not inconsistent with the purpose of the Act or the requirements imposed under relevant Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement adequacy criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether provisions for enforcement of the applicant State law are adequate, consideration will be given to the extent to which provision is made for administrative enforcement, including necessary facilities, personnel, and funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties back to the supporting documentation showing fiscal arrangements, staffing, and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and proposed rule publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial review of a filed application, a proposed rule concerning the application for exemption will be published by the Bureau in the Federal Register, and a copy of such application will be made available for examination by interested persons. A comment period will be allowed from the date of such publication for interested parties to submit written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption issuance procedure and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Bureau determines that an applicant State law is substantially similar and provides adequate enforcement, a final rule granting the exemption will be published in the Federal Register, copies furnished to relevant officials, and any exemption granted will be effective 90 days after the date of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: State notification of changes post-exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State that receives an exemption must inform the Assistant Director in writing within 30 days of any change in the applicant State law, including copies of the full text of that change and statements setting forth specified information and opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report of any change must contain the same types of materials required in the initial application (per paragraph III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic reporting requirement after exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide, not later than two years after the date the exemption is granted, and every two years thereafter, a report to the Bureau concerning the manner in which the State has enforced the applicant State law in the preceding two years and an update of the information required under paragraph III(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau notification of statutory/regulatory amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau will inform any State that receives such an exemption of any subsequent amendments of the Act or this part that might necessitate the amendment of State law for the exemption to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclusive effect of State law after exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: After an exemption is granted, the requirements of the applicable State law constitute the requirements of relevant Federal law, except to the extent such State law imposes requirements not imposed by the Act or this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse determination process
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Bureau cannot make a favorable determination, it will notify the appropriate State official of the facts upon which such findings are based and will afford the State authority a reasonable opportunity to submit additional materials demonstrating the basis for granting an exemption; if still unfavorable, the Bureau will publish a final rule containing its determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation criteria and process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau reserves the right to revoke any exemption if it determines the State law does not impose requirements substantially similar to relevant Federal law or that there is not adequate provision for State enforcement. Before revoking, the Bureau will notify the State of the facts or conduct and afford opportunity to demonstrate continued eligibility; if not remedied, a proposed rule to revoke will be published with a comment period and, if revoked, a final rule will be published and revocation becomes effective 90 days after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory opinions — protection for good-faith conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act done or omitted in good faith in conformity with any advisory opinion issued by the Bureau provides the protection afforded under section 813(e) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau will amend the appendix periodically to incorporate references to advisory opinions issued; advisory opinions will be published in the Federal Register and on consumerfinance.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for advisory opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an advisory opinion may be submitted in accordance with the instructions regarding submission and content of requests applicable to any relevant advisory opinion program that the Bureau offers; requests will be reviewed consistent with that program's process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official interpretations — request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone may request that an official interpretation of the regulation be added to the commentary. A request must be in writing and addressed to the Assistant Director and must contain a complete statement of all relevant facts, including copies of all pertinent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions adopted in accordance with rulemaking procedures will be incorporated following publication in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment designations in Supplement I
rubrics_metrics.description: Each comment in the commentary is identified by a number and the regulatory section or paragraph that it interprets; comments are designated with as much specificity as possible (e.g., comment 6(d)(4)(i)-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This introduction may be cited as comments I-1, I-2, and I-3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Attempt To Communicate
rubrics_metrics.description: An attempt to communicate is any act to initiate a communication or other contact about a debt with any person through any medium, including by soliciting a response from such person; an attempt to communicate occurs regardless of whether successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: placing a call (reached or not) or leaving voicemail are attempts to communicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Communicate or Communication (any medium)
rubrics_metrics.description: A communication can occur through any medium, including oral, written, electronic, or other media; a communication means conveying information regarding a debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include in-person contact, telephone calls, audio recordings, paper documents, mail, email, text, social media, or other electronic media. Marketing/advertising that does not contain information about a specific debt is not a communication under §1006.2(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Debt (consumer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt means, in part, any obligation or alleged obligation of a consumer to pay money arising out of a transaction, and consumer means any natural person obligated or allegedly obligated to pay any debt; only natural persons can incur debts as defined in §1006.2(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Debt Collector
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector is any person who uses any instrumentality of interstate commerce or mail in any business the principal purpose of which is the collection of debts, or who regularly collects or attempts to collect, directly or indirectly, debts owed or due, or asserted to be owed or due, to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who collects defaulted debts that the person has purchased but who does not have a business the principal purpose of which is debt collection and who does not collect debts owed to another is not a debt collector as defined in §1006.2(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Limited-Content Message (voicemail)
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited-content message is a voicemail message for a consumer that includes all of the content described in §1006.2(j)(1), may include any of the content described in §1006.2(j)(2), and includes no other content. Any other message is not a limited-content message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If voicemail includes content beyond those items and that content directly or indirectly conveys information about a debt, it is a communication under §1006.2(d). Messages knowingly left for third parties are not limited-content messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful disclosure and limited-content messages
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector who leaves only a limited-content message for a consumer does not violate §1006.14(g)'s requirement to meaningfully disclose the caller's identity with respect to that voicemail message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-content message — required content example
rubrics_metrics.description: Example of required content that constitutes a limited-content message: “This is Robin Smith calling from ABC Inc. Please contact me or Jim Johnson at 1-800-555-1212.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-content message — optional content limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited-content message may include a statement that, if the consumer replies, the consumer may speak to any of the company's representatives or associates, but a more detailed description of the representative group (e.g., “credit card receivables group”) is not a limited-content message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of optional content combined with required content: providing call-times and phone number while indicating any representative may answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(a) — who counts as a consumer for communications rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §1006.6, the term consumer includes a consumer's spouse; the consumer's parent if the consumer is a minor; and the executor/administrator/personal representative of a deceased consumer's estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal representative includes persons authorized to act on behalf of the deceased consumer's estate including those under informal probate, universal successors, or those who sign declarations to transfer estate assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(b)(1) — Prohibition on communicating at unusual or inconvenient times/places
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1006.6(b)(1) prohibits a debt collector from communicating or attempting to communicate about a debt at a time or place that the debt collector knows or should know is inconvenient to the consumer, unless an exception in §1006.6(b)(4) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples explain that prior notes from a creditor, consumer statements like “I am busy,” or explicit statements that home is off-limits qualify as knowledge. Debt collector may ask follow-up questions to clarify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer-initiated communication — one-response rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If a consumer initiates a communication from a time/place previously designated inconvenient, the debt collector may respond once at that time/place through the same medium; after that response, further communications are prohibited unless consumer says time/place is no longer inconvenient or an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include email replies while within an inconvenient time window, telephone calls from a previously-off-limits place, and interactions while consumer navigates a website/mobile app (automated replies permitted once).

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(b)(1)(i) — Time of electronic communication and default inconvenient times
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic communications, an electronic communication occurs when the debt collector sends it. In absence of knowledge to the contrary, an inconvenient time is before 8:00 a.m. and after 9:00 p.m. local time at the consumer's location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If debt collector has ambiguous/conflicting information about consumer's location, it must pick a time convenient in all indicated locations (examples with time zone calculations provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(b)(1)(ii) — Unusual or inconvenient places and media association
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collector must not communicate through media associated with an unusual place or a place the debt collector knows or should know is inconvenient (mailing addresses, landlines are associated with a place). Email addresses and mobile telephone numbers are not associated with a place unless the debt collector knows the consumer is at an unusual/inconvenient place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: calling a consumer's mobile or sending email does not violate the place prohibition even if the consumer happens to view while at home, unless the collector knows the consumer is at home and home is an inconvenient place.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(b)(2) — Communications when consumer represented by an attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: A consumer-initiated communication from a consumer represented by an attorney constitutes the consumer's prior consent to that communication so the debt collector may respond once, but that act does not negate knowledge that the consumer is represented nor revoke protections; after response, the collector must not communicate further unless it knows the consumer is not represented with respect to the debt or an exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(b)(3) — Communications at place of employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1006.6(b)(3) prohibits a debt collector from communicating at a consumer's place of employment if the collector knows or has reason to know that the consumer's employer prohibits the consumer from receiving such communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A debt collector has reason to know if the consumer says they cannot take personal calls at work. Collector may ask follow-up questions. Special rules address employer-provided email (see §1006.22(f)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(b)(4)(i) — Prior consent exception (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibitions in §§1006.6(b)(1)–(3) do not apply if the debt collector communicates with the prior consent of the consumer. The collector may ask during a communication what time/place would be convenient but may not ask the consumer to consent to the continuation of that inconvenient communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior consent must be voluntary and not elicited as a condition of continuing the same inconvenient call/communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(b)(4)(ii) — Prior consent must be given directly to collector
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1006.6(b)(4)(i) requires the prior consent of the consumer to be given directly to the debt collector; a debt collector cannot rely on the consumer's prior consent given to a creditor or to a previous debt collector.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1006.6(c)(1) — Refusal to pay or cease communication notice completion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If a consumer notifies a debt collector in writing or electronically that the consumer refuses to pay a debt or wants the debt collector to cease further communication, notification is complete upon the debt collector's receipt of that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a mailed written notification is effective upon receipt; communications sent before receipt do not violate the rule. Comment interprets E-SIGN Act to allow electronic requests to satisfy the 'in writing' requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-SIGN Act interpretation for §1006.6(c)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Bureau's interpretation, section 101(a) of the E-SIGN Act enables a consumer to satisfy the FDCPA requirement that the consumer's notification be 'in writing' through an electronic request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means electronic submissions via a medium the debt collector accepts count as written notices for purposes of cease communications/refusal-to-pay notices.
